change_summary: Ran a runtime-only deterministic stress-state experiment using the three fixed OHLCV snapshots. First audited the trigger counts per window, then monkey-patched sizing so that only on `stress_strict` days the portfolio risk budget was multiplied by `0.5x` or `0.25x`. Entries, exits, ranking, strategy mix, and all accepted A+B cohort rules stayed unchanged. No repository trading logic was kept after measurement.
component: runtime-only monkeypatch of `BacktestEngine._earnings_dict_for` + `portfolio_engine.size_signals()` to apply a same-day gross-risk haircut keyed off a cached strict stress-date map (rolled back; no repo trading logic changed)

delta_metrics.note: The AND semantics successfully fixed the over-fire failure mode from exp-20260423-013, but the deployment still failed Gate 4. Both strict variants stayed a complete null in the late and middle windows, and only the oldest weak window improved modestly. This means the remaining blocker is no longer state-definition width; it is that a single-stage gross-risk haircut is too blunt to convert weak-tape detection into stable multi-window alpha.

hypothesis: If the rejected broad OR-based stress template failed because its semantics were too loose, then a much narrower conjunctive risk-state should recover the useful part of the meta-layer idea: define `stress_strict` only when `breadth_above_200 <= 0.55` AND `spy_pct_from_ma <= -0.02`, and then apply a modest gross-risk haircut on those days. A valid rule should stay near-silent in the late-strong window while improving the weaker windows.

market_regime_summary.late_strong: slow-melt bull with brief Mar-2026 stress pocket
market_regime_summary.mid_weak: bullish / rotation-heavy tape with early-window pressure cluster
market_regime_summary.old_thin: mixed-to-weak tape culminating in Mar-Apr 2025 macro stress

next_retry_requires: Do not retry nearby `0.5x/0.25x/0.0x` gross-risk sweeps on the same `breadth_above_200 + spy_pct_from_ma` strict state by default

If this weak-tape branch returns, require either an explicit two-stage design where strict stress detection drives a sleeve-specific action, or a genuinely richer state that adds another independent context source such as volatility or flow
Treat this result as a doctrine update: risk-state detection and risk-state action are separate questions; fixing the trigger semantics alone is not enough
notes: Single-causal-variable discipline held relative to exp-20260423-013: the action family remained a same-day gross-risk haircut, while the only intended change was the state-definition semantics (broad OR -> strict AND). The audit showed late-window trigger scarcity exactly as intended, so this is a clean rejection of the action shape, not another over-triggering false negative.

deployment.action_scope: all signals on stress days only

rejection_reason: Rejected on Gate 4 multi-window stability. The strict conjunctive stress detector is cleaner than the rejected OR form, but it still does not produce majority-window improvement. The family now looks measurement-clean but action-weak: same-day gross-risk haircuts on strict weak-tape days are too blunt and too sparse to justify repo-level promotion.
